statements.status_notes: GnuPG can be made to spin on a relatively small input by (for example) crafting a public key with thousands of signatures attached, compressed down to just a few KB.
statements.impact_statement: GnuPG can be made to spin/consume excessive CPU on a relatively small input, such as a crafted public key with thousands of signatures compressed into a few KB (explicit upstream won't-fix). No gpg/gnupg/dirmngr invocation exists anywhere in this image's runtime.
GnuPG binary package. GnuPG is installed for build-time package signature verification only; not invoked at runtime by Liquibase.

statements.status_notes: CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax) parsing in gpgsm in GnuPG through 2.5.20 mishandles the CMS format for AES-GCM because aes-ICVlen is supposed to be 12 bytes but 4 bytes is accepted. NOTE: this is related to CVE-2026-34182.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in Ubuntu package 2.4.4-2ubuntu17.6. The vulnerable path is in GnuPG CMS parsing through gpgsm/dirmngr handling of AES-GCM CMS input. Liquibase Secure's shipped runtime does not invoke gpgsm, dirmngr, or related GnuPG tooling, so the affected CMS parser is not exercised by the application surface.
